posts.contents:
Dear Abby,

Thanks for reaching out regarding Reece Knight's XP in AlphaWrite. There is currently an ongoing outage (see status page [https://alphaschool.statuspage.io/]) affecting metrics visibility, which is likely causing the discrepancy.

Upon reviewing the student’s activity over the past week, we noted the following XP mismatches:

	* 09/24

	* Timeback shows 15 XP (suggesting 1 completed lesson in 100%)
	* AlphaWrite app shows 5 fully completed lessons, which should amount to 75 XP

	* 09/23

	* Timeback shows 15 XP (suggesting 1 completed lesson in 100%)
	* AlphaWrite app shows 4 fully completed lessons, which should amount to 60 XP

Regarding 09/29, where you mentioned the student should have received 45 XP, we did not find any lesson marked as 100% complete. The only lesson started on that date, "Turn Outline into Draft", appears to have been completed on 09/30. This aligns with the 60 XP (for 4 completed lessons) reflected in Timeback for that day.

We’ll escalate the discrepancies for the other dates to the appropriate team to ensure XP is correctly displayed. We’ll keep you updated as soon as we have more information.

Best regards,
Michael Galicha
EDU Support Team

posts.contents:
Dear Joshua,

We reviewed Karthik’s activity and can confirm that he did complete lessons on September 29, as seen in the Lalilo Dashboard and supporting records. However, the XP credit for that work is not showing in TimeBack.

Under usual circumstances, we would escalate this to the team that manages the Lalilo–TimeBack integration. At this time, though, the TimeBack team is already addressing a known issue impacting XP reporting, which is also being tracked on the Alpha status page. We recommend subscribing to the Alpha status page for updates: Alpha Status Page [https://alphaschool.statuspage.io]. Subscribing will ensure that you receive direct notifications by email whenever new updates are posted.

[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/365A4BOd86nBfHjYkM8QuiE8Hx58hd4A" width="46.98%" style="width: 46.98%;" height="352.141"]

If the issue continues after the TimeBack team confirms the problem is resolved, please reply to this ticket. At that point, we can investigate further and backfill any missed credits for Karthik.

For now, we expect this to be resolved directly by the TimeBack team, and updates will be shared via the Alpha status page.

Please let us know if you have any other questions or concerns in the meantime.

Best regards,
Syed Haider
EDU Support Team

This ticket will stay open for one week unless you reply with "This ticket can be closed" or update the status to Completed in the portal. We will write to you again to remind you.

posts.subject: XP Tracking Issue - Math
posts.contents:
Dear Kelvin,

Greetings from EDU Support. This ticket was raised on your behalf to review Comerson Allen's Math metrics and look for tracking issues. 

We are glad to report that Comerson's progress is being tracked correctly for this app. As indicated in the Zearn Guide Manual [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CT8naD99xcIcs4ZMyxu1TJaEGIT5FpF66GpOBulUux0/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.qipixfpkt64o], students are awarded XP after they finish the last activity in a lesson (“Tower of Power” quiz) as long as they didn't receive a "Tower of Power Alert" (for getting an answer wrong 3 times in a row). 

Comerson completed one lesson yesterday (Sep 29th) and one today, and they've received the corresponding 15 XP for each as indicated in the interactive XP Guide [https://cms.academics.alpha.school/2hrlearning-xp-guide] for G3 lessons. It is also very important to remember that students should always sign in with the credentials in TimeBack for their progress to be tracked correctly, they should never use Google SSO (this doesn't seem to have been a problem for Comerson so far, but it's still worth mentioning). 

Finally, we'd like to take this chance to highlight that data tracking delays of at least 1 hour are normal and expected for this app; this is a limitation of the platform, so data collection can't be expedited.

We hope this covers what you needed for Math (other subjects are being reviewed separately), but please let us know if you need anything else from our end at this time. Thank you! 

Best regards,
Alonso Aguirre
EDU Support Team

This ticket will stay open for one week unless you reply with "This ticket can be closed" or update the status to Completed in the portal. We will write to you again to remind you.

posts.contents:
Proposed Team:

 	* Academics Reading

 		Affected students:

 	*  Lucas Sanner (September 25)

 		Affected apps:

 	*  AlphaRead

 		Presumed DRI:

 	* Alex Wrega
 	* Ilma Cohadzic

 What is the issue reported? 

How does this affect the student? :

 	* In the lesson The Departure of Sir Lancelot, quiz question 1/5 is providing contradictory feedback. The explanation indicates that an answer is correct, but the application marks it as incorrect when the correction appears on screen.

	* How does this affect the student? 

 	* From a technical perspective, the QTI resource for this quiz item has the qti-correct-response pointing to an answer option that is not aligned with what the explanation feedback communicates. Because AlphaRead is pulling the “correct” value directly from the QTI database, the system enforces the wrong correctness logic.
 	* For the student, this results in confusion and unfair scoring: they may answer correctly according to the explanation provided, but still be marked as incorrect, affecting their overall performance and learning experience.

 		What investigation did CS carry out? :

 	* Verified the issue in AlphaRead with affected student: Lucas Sanner (Sep 25).

	* Gathered screenshots: 

 	* Screenshot 1 [https://i.ibb.co/FkMWJBXd/image.png] 
 	* Screenshot 2 [https://i.ibb.co/YTNtj1fh/image.png] 

 	* Engaged AE Studio team, who confirmed the issue lies in the QTI content, not the AlphaRead application.
 	* QTI resource link: quiz_303353 [https://qti.alpha-1edtech.com/api/assessment-items/quiz_303353] 
 	* Extracted raw XML confirming the qti-correct-response is tied to the choice “Sir Gawaine has lost his ability to think clearly”.

 		What is requested of Academics?

 	* Please review and correct the content in the QTI resource so that the designated correct answer and feedback align properly. Once the content is fixed, CS can coordinate with AE Studio to retroactively update student responses in timeback-db so that affected students’ scores are corrected.

 		Other notes:

   

 	* This is not an isolated case; AE Studio observed multiple similar issues today, possibly due to recent content updates.

posts.contents:
The problem lies in the content itself and not in the application. The application (AlphaRead) is displaying the incorrect answer as correct because it is how it is set up in the resource which comes from the QTI database. 

 The correct answer value is pointing to 'Sir Gawaine has lost his ability to think clearly.' and the QTI resource can be viewed here: https://qti.alpha-1edtech.com/api/assessment-items/quiz_303353 

  Additionally, I have pulled the specific xml snippets from the resource to show the correct-response value that the system sees:  

<qti-correct-response><qti-value>answer_603310</qti-value></qti-correct-response>

<qti-simple-choice identifier=answer_603310>
Sir Gawaine has lost his ability to think clearly.
<qti-feedback-inline outcome-identifier=FEEDBACK-INLINE identifier=answer_603310 
show-hide=show>You successfully made a smart inference by noticing that Gawaine isn’t 
thinking clearly. The text supports this when it says, “In his madness, Sir Gawaine refused 
to listen to King Arthur,” and that he “did not care if the entire army would perish…as 
long as he could get his revenge.” Remember to look for strong clue words about a character’s
actions and feelings (like “madness” or “refused to listen”) to figure out what they are 
thinking.</qti-feedback-inline>
</qti-simple-choice>

 The owner of this particular question and content is ilma.cohadzic@trilogy.com, and we believe the best course of action is to reach out to Ilma regarding the content and any updates that need to be made to the content. 

 Once that is done, we can retroactively update student responses in timeback-db so the scores reflect the correct information for a provided list of affected students.

Also to over-communicate, we have seen several of these issues come through today and it seems there were updates made to some of the content pieces. What I have done to investigate is look directly at the questions rawXml value in the QTI database (the url above) which has shown me where the issue we see in this ticket originates from.  

 Please let us know if you have any additional questions.

Thank you very much for your patience as we looked into the feedback mismatch issue in the Grade 12 AlphaRead passages.

The developers have reviewed the video and attempted to replicate the issue, but were unable to do so. Based on their review and similar past reports, they believe the root cause might have already been fixed by the recently released updates.

Best regards,

José Guedes

posts.contents:
Hey all,

I went through and attempt to replicate the reported issue exactly as shown in the video and was unsuccessful. It appears there were some updates pushed to the content by an external team and it has corrected what appeared to me to be misaligned inline-feedback XML identifiers. Loom video link: https://www.loom.com/share/ef46a0827b3d418192942100867409e6 

To over-communicate, there are two types of feedback set in the xml we are seeing. First, it the correct/incorrect message (the single word that says That's right!. Second, is the inline feedback which gives the student a large explanation for the chosen answer. The issue, I can assume from other similar tickets submitted to us, is there was a misalignment in the identifiers used for inline feedback within the content's xml.

I went in and verified the student's answers in Timeback-API as well as a secondary verification in AlphaRead DB. I did not see the final answer in the video that was sent, but the student was given the proper scores in both dbs. 

 To conclude, the content was updated to show the student the proper feedback by the content owner, and the student's answers saved in the database were marked correctly.

posts.contents:
Good morning,
There are a few ways in  how Alpha Read (https://alpharead.alpha.school -- the one without timeback integration) handles article recommendations:
1 - The user is enrolled in one or more power path courses:
1.1 - the system will pick the preferred enrolled course specified in the guide admin page for that student
1.2 - if no preferred course is available, the system will try matching the enrolled power path courses to the age grade and knowledge/reading grade of the student (knowledge grade and age grade are found in the student's profile)
1.3 - if there is no preferred enrolled course, and there are no matches in terms of grade to the courses the student in enrolled in, the system will fallback to show recommended articles (see item 2)
2 - The user is not enrolled in power path: in this case the system will show the student recommended articles for their age grade and knowledge/reading grade. This way the system will always show recommended articles to students unless they have read and done activities for all articles available.

posts.subject: The problem lies in the content itself and not in the application. The application is displaying the incorrect answer as correct because it is how it is set up in the resource. Both the setup and the content need to be updated to reflect the actual corre...
posts.contents:
The problem lies in the content itself and not in the application. The application is displaying the incorrect answer as correct because it is how it is set up in the resource. Both the setup and the content need to be updated to reflect the actual correct answer. You can see in the xml snippets below, the correct answer value is pointing to 'Children should always to their chores and never hide' - https://qti.alpha-1edtech.com/api/assessment-items/quiz_302760

The specific xml snippets:
<qti-correct-response> 
 <qti-value>answer_603138</qti-value> 
 </qti-correct-response> 

 <qti-simple-choice identifier=answer_603138>        Children should always do their chores and never hide.        <qti-feedback-inline outcome-identifier=FEEDBACK-INLINE identifier=answer_603138 show-hide=show>You successfully identified the lesson by noticing that Alemeda tries to hide but is reminded that doing her work matters. The text supports this when her mother says, “We need you. We have work to do. We must finish the baskets,” and Grandma explains they must store food to “survive when winter comes.” Remember: when finding a lesson, look at what the character does at the start and what they learn by the end, and underline quotes that show why the behavior (like doing chores) is important.</qti-feedback-inline>      </qti-simple-choice> 

The owner of this particular question and content is: ilma.cohadzic@trilogy.com

The best course of action is to reach out to Ilma to correct the content. Once that is done, we can retroactively update student responses in timeback-db so their scores reflect the correct information.

posts.contents:
I'll just add some notes for documentation purposes as the issue was initially reported as data not tracking correctly. I spent a long time reviewing this as it's not super straightforward with the tools we have. But this is the short version after checking thoroughly.  

 The main issue is that Elena worked on repeated, already-mastered lessons. So, this is not a tracking issue, it's user error. This was the status of their Writing course in TimeBack on Sep 15th before they started working on lessons, and they mastered many of them but as you can see, they had already been mastered before. Same thing happened on Sep 16th, the courses hadn't been refreshed and they just completed lessons from the same already-completed courses once more, and got no XP from it; there are Caliper events for the work done and they include XP, it's just not awarded in TimeBack.  
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/mjC5FvYtVRyAZ7yPL0ZTlrbWXYiAZSAM" width="1079" height="1035"] 

 Now, as you can see from the screenshot above, one lesson was still In Progress (i.e., not yet mastered). There was one more in Paragraphs G3 which she also had in TimeBack, and she mastered both. Still, Elena didn't get any XP from those lessons as even those had already been mastered before.  
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/qB9yacfTxUrQPElpNGBWnCNTP8xDP6oX" width="1079" height="945"] 

 See for example the event_time and Caliper event 'generated' for Write Questions About a Picture in Sentences G3; it was originally mastered on August 14th (and then a few other times on 09/10th, 11th, 15th, and 22nd.   
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/ckxUvcvjv6D40BG2rOl6filOwCRIWqWO" width="1079" height="212"] 

 But it doesn't make much sense to me that the course/lesson would be assigned again, unless this was a conscious decision made by Academics, in which case I do hope they considered Elena wouldn't receive XP for this upon remastery.  

 That's what I will escalate now, I couldn't find recent tickets discussing Elena's placement in Writing, so I have no more details to review at this time.  
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/gYshiM8nYWXkgwebat0WjeQTtb4ZcnGt"]

Hi Tripti,

Christina’s account now has access to the Santa Barbara students as requested.

Just to clarify, the current process requires students to be assigned manually to an aide in order for them to view and monitor their Learning Metrics. While this works, we recognize it can become time-consuming when an aide supports a larger group of students.

The good news is that the product team is actively working on a new feature that will allow guides to be assigned by level, so that all students in that level will be automatically linked. This will eliminate the need for manual assignments in the future.

In the meantime, if you need aides to have visibility over many students at once, let us know so we can make the changes in the backend for those aides to ensure they can view all relevant students without adding them individually.

Please let us know if there is anything else we can help you with.

Best regards,
Xavier A Villarroel
EDU Support Team

posts.contents:
Hi Randall, 

 Thanks for raising this. Currently, it’s not incorrect to manually assign students to an aide, but this process can become very time-consuming when an aide is working with a large group of students. 

 We’re actively working on a new feature that will allow guides to be assigned a level, and all students in that level will automatically be connected to them. This will remove the need for manual student-by-student assignments. 

 In the meantime, most teams have been using a short-term workaround by granting guides admin access, which ensures they can view all students without needing each one added manually. 

 For future cases where an aide needs access to many students, we recommend using the admin access workaround until the new feature is released. 

 Best, 
 William

posts.contents:
Thank you for providing the information. After reviewing the registration details for each user, we found that Teacher Samantha currently holds the following roles:
– Teacher at Alpha School Orlando
– Administrator at Alpha School Miami
– Student at Guide School (listed twice) 
 Fernando, on the other hand, is an administrator in several organizations, including Alpha Anywhere Center, where the three students are registered. 
 Please note that Teacher Samantha has restricted access to view only the students enrolled in the same classes and organizations as she is. To allow her to view these students, we recommend changing her role to Aide within the same organization as the students (Alpha Anywhere Center). 
 You can actually set this up yourself through the UI. Here’s how: 

 	* Log into your admin account
 	* Go to Administration → Users
 	* Search for the user whose role you want to change
 	* In the Actions menu, click View Details
 	* Change the role to Aide for the school they’re in
 	* Add the students this aide will be responsible for

 This way, the guide will be able to view student learning metrics and impersonate the student. 
 Let me know if you run into any issues, I’ll be happy to help! 
 Best, 
 Natalia

Kindly note that Fernando and Jose were unable to see the students because it seems that the behavior has changed and our admin access didn't grant us access to all campuses anymore. They were able to see the students after I specifically added a role for them as administrators of the specific campus.  

 For Samantha, we are aware that we can make students available to her by adding them one by one to her account, but why did they disappear in the first place? And why did this happen today specifically? It looks like some changes were introduced today in TimeBack's behavior, but changes that made teachers unable to see students not specifically added to their account (for Teacher and Aide roles, for example) had already been introduced several days ago, so why was the Guide able to see their students in the morning and not anymore after a while?

 		 Hope this reaches you well. We received a report of what seems to be a glitch in the feedback for the lesson Caliban by J. P. Dancing Bear [https://alpharead.alpha-1edtech.com/admin/articles?articleId=117254].
When answering the question: “Which pairing best captures the speaker’s conflicted attitude toward his mother in the poem?”, the system correctly marked “resentful of her choices, yet loving toward her” as the right answer. However, the feedback displayed under the incorrect answer option claimed:
“This option is incorrect because the passage is not provided, so we cannot determine…”
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/uYimwC8pWxkPNz8GnQd6QaBPgl8tfmvS" width="414" height="487"]

Note that the above is from my own test which is the same same feedback as what the student reported.

This seems inconsistent because the passage was, in fact, provided earlier in the lesson. The explanation reads as though the system didn’t have access to the text, even though the correct interpretation was based on it.

Interestingly, when using the admin (one with dev tools enabled), the system did provide valid feedback.[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/dRu24L5zEdFq8DvLxhhKtsOuCSRZi5d6"]

Could you please review this behavior? It might be a case of the wrong feedback template being triggered or a mismatch between answer logic and the feedback script.

 		 Possible Glitch in Feedback for Caliban Lesson by J. P. Dancing Bear - https://alpharead.alpha-1edtech.com/admin/articles?articleId=117254

posts.contents:
Hi Randall, 

 As I mentioned in my previous message, the issue comes from ClearFluency sending 11 TimeSpent events on 09/17, which added up to 115 minutes. For the time to show correctly in TimeBack, ClearFluency would need to adjust what they send, either by overwriting the existing TimeSpent values using the same event_id they originally sent or by sending new events that subtract the overcounted time (for example, -10 seconds). 

 Unfortunately, we cannot make that adjustment on our side. If we changed the data directly, it would break consistency for everyone else who consumes the same events. The correction really needs to come from the source so that all downstream systems stay in sync. 

 That way, the corrected total would align with the actual 23 minutes observed. 

 Best, 
 William

> #taro-issue-summary

 The customer facing defect involves G3 Writing tests in MasteryTrack incorrectly awarding 90 XP instead of the expected 30 XP, affecting 29 student events since September 16, 2025, including student McKayla Caldbeck. The root cause was identified in the MasteryTrack backend service where a COALESCE function in the SQL query defaulted to 90 XP when test metadata XP values were missing, rather than using the correct grade and subject-based calculation that should award 30 XP for G3 Writing tests. The Engineering team has implemented a fix by updating the authoring service SQL query to use proper CASE statement logic that calculates XP based on grade_rank and subject instead of the hardcoded 90 default, and BeyondAI has confirmed the problematic test has been deactivated, but Customer Support should note that retroactive correction of XP values for the 29 affected events still needs to be completed. 

TICKET SUMMARY: MCKAYLA CALDBECK - EXCESSIVE XP FOR WRITING

ISSUE STATUS: RESOLVED (ENGINEERING FIX COMPLETE)

 Key Details: 

 	* Ticket: McKayla Caldbeck - Excessive XP for Writing
 	* Issue: G3 Writing tests awarding 90 XP instead of 30 XP
 	* Affected Students: 29 total events since September 16, 2025
 	* Root Cause: MasteryTrack backend configuration error in SQL query fallback logic
 	* Engineering Fix: ✅ COMPLETED - BeyondAI has fixed the code and deactivated the problematic test

CURRENT STATUS ANALYSIS

 ✅ What's Been Resolved: 

 	* Root Cause Identified: SQL query in authoring.service.ts had incorrect COALESCE fallback (90 XP instead of proper grade-based calculation)
 	* Code Fix Implemented: BeyondAI updated the SQL query to use proper CASE statement logic
 	* Problematic Test Deactivated: The specific test causing issues has been removed
 	* Future Prevention: New tests will use correct XP calculation logic

 ⚠️ What Still Needs Attention: 

 	* Retroactive XP Correction: The 29 affected student events still need XP values corrected from 90 to 30

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS FOR SUPPORT TEAM

posts.contents:
This happened because Kelvin has an Aide role and is not related to any students. Some students need to be linked to his account for him to have access to metrics.

To do that, anyone with an Admin access should access the User page, search for the user and tap the View Details actions option:

[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/A7EwBryY5J9ex0BzF98p4twlbY3qNuGC"]

After clicking on the option, they'll be able to start adding students to his control by clicking on the Add Student button:

[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/O6MyO3HSss0mY616o1dwKTYOGWH96Nbt"]

The other users' emails mentioned on the ticket already have an Admin role, so they should not face this error, we released a fix to avoid this check for admins.

On the next release, we'll be updating the way Guides have access to students, they'll receive access to students on certain Alpha Levels (L1, L2 etc).

 	* Potentially others

 		Affected dates:

 		N/A

 		Evidence:

 		Checking Jack first, the Dashboard expects a total of 937 XP and 156 Mastered Units (EMUs) in Language session to date to considered students to be learning at 2X pace (this is the sum of earned and required to catch up metrics).

There have been 23 week days in total counting August 13th and today (September 12th); I'm considering this to be the total for now, but arguably we may want to exclude holidays, MAP week, and any other days in which students can't/don't actually work in core skills. But anyway, for the sake of the exercise, let's say they are expected to earn XP and EMUs every single week day, Monday to Friday, so 23 days in this session so far.

That is 40.739 XP and 6.78 Mastered Units daily.
Jack is only enrolled in 1 Language app, expectations shown in Learning Metrics page are 25 XP and 2 mastered units.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/7UOfQLLNY4qL0uSzmC8TPwIQc67P2CAG" width="652" height="454"]

If we extrapolate to 23 school days, the real goal would be 575 XP and 46 Mastered Units. This would place Jack at roughly 163% XP and 339% Mastered Units session to date, instead of the numbers they have currently.

The situation is similar for Jonathan, who has the exact same goals displayed in their Learning Metrics (25 XP and 2 EMUs daily), and who currently has 546 XP and 47 EMUs session to date according to their Learning Report, which would place them at around 95% XP and 102% EMUs, yet they currently show 58% XP and 30% EMUs.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/lzROEsEi0egfh3iCjlqTIAFH1Qq636pP" width="979" height="911"]

 		Reason for Escalation:

 	* Please investigate, find the root cause, and implement a fix. 

	* If possible, please share details on how this is supposed to work and how it is calculated so that we can effectively Support Guides and students in the future.  

 	* For example, does it consider all days even if students started school late (not since the start of the session), does it omit weekends and holidays, does it omit MAP Week, does it change if students are enrolled in more than one app per subject, etc. 

Thank you!

 		Language

 		What is the issue reported?

How does this affect the student? :
 		Learning Reports in Timeback for Aero Guadagno show incorrect values for XP and Mastered Units in the Language -> Mentava course , with unrealistic percentages (1,249,600% XP and 312,400% Mastered Units). This discrepancy arises because the Mentava course does not have the total XP and total lessons set yet in Timeback -> Manage Metrics setting.

From a technical POV, the absence of total XP and lessons leads to the system calculating values that should be 0, but actual events with XP and completed lessons are being reported from the client app. This results in misleading metrics that can confuse students and guides, affecting the student's understanding of their progress and performance in the course.

 		What investigation did CS carry out? :
 		CS reviewed the reported metrics and confirmed that the XP values and lessons are inconsistent with what is shown on the dashboard. The underlying issue was identified after escalating to the AE Studio team, being that the Mentava course lacked the necessary total XP and total lessons value set in Timeback -> Manage Metrics setting.

 		What is requested of Academics?
 		Please review and provide the correct values for the total XP and total lessons expected to be set for the Language -> Mentava course in Timeback.

This will allow us to modify the calculations accordingly and avoid future discrepancies.
Note: Academics Language advised that they do not have Mentava for k-2 so we are asking reading team (Nick) to check if they can help

Thank you for reaching out and for your patience as we investigate the issue with the “Essential Lessons Mastered vs. Target” report in the My Learning Report dashboard. 

 We understand how confusing and frustrating it can be to see sudden, unexplained changes in XP requirements, especially when setting learning goals and tracking student progress. 

 Our team is currently working on a full refactor of this report to ensure the data is accurate, reliable, and easy to understand. We’re collaborating with stakeholders to confirm which metrics should be displayed and how best to structure the report for clarity and consistency. 

 In the meantime, we recommend disregarding the XP requirement figures shown in the dashboard until the updated version is released. We’ll keep you informed as soon as improvements are live. 

 Thank you again for bringing this to our attention.

Hello,

The automated enrollments  (as being called in alpha read), are created when our system (Alpha Read) receives a request for the https://alpharead.alpha.school/recommendations/links [https://alpharead.alpha.school/recommendations/links?email=gustavo.higuchi@ae.studio&age_grade=5&knowledge_grade=3&limit=50] endpoint (e.g. https://alpharead.alpha.school/recommendations/links?email=gustavo.higuchi@ae.studio&age_grade=5&knowledge_grade=3&limit=50). This endpoint will search powerpath for a course matching the details provided and enroll the student.

It's our understanding that the application responsible for making requests to that endpoint is known as Dash.

Once you review the details being sent from Dash to our Alpha read endpoint, and you want the automated enrollments to work again, please toggle the bypass manual enrollment inside Alpha Read's student management page, otherwise the student will keep seeing articles for the course that was manually set for him.

I sent this in Slack: 

 Hi DJ, 

 Initial data 

 	* A clip from Lawson's screen recordings showing this clearly [https://main-worksmart-clips-0002md.s3.amazonaws.com/clips/2840876/1757618812927_063f3445-dbe9-452b-8bce-a93511a5979b.mp4] 
 	* Article link: Don Quixote and Sancho Panza Have Some Strange Adventures [https://alpharead.alpha-1edtech.com/articles?articleId=103036&crsid=article_103036] 
 	* Screenshot of the question:
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/SWT8ERAyYyD7zWQA2AloVKbQa0AZV5kZ" width="666" height="465"]

 Interpreting what happened 

 	* Option B (“You must now go to El Toboso…”) doesn’t really show Don Quixote’s confused view of reality but rather his devotion to Dulcinea.
 	* Option D (“That’s a disguise, but you can’t hide from me.”) is the correct answer because it directly shows his confused belief — Don Quixote thinks innocent friars are disguised wizards.

 The explanation for students who select option B says: 

> This option is incorrect because while this quotation shows Don Quixote's strange behavior, it doesn't directly demonstrate his confused view of reality as clearly as option B does. This quote focuses more on his commands and his devotion to Dulcinea rather than showing how he misunderstands what he sees.

 I highlighted a typo in the explanation. It should have said “option D” (the correct answer), not “option B.” Because of this slip, the wording looks like it’s contradicting itself. 
 So the intended explanation was: 

> …it doesn't directly demonstrate his confused view of reality as clearly as option D does...

 How to reassure Lawson 

> “You were right to notice that something didn’t add up. The explanation for option B has a small typo — it accidentally says ‘option B’ when it meant ‘option D.’ 
>  Option D is the one that shows Don Quixote’s confused reality most clearly. Option B is arguably odd, but it's not showcasing any confusion between reality and what Don Quixote is seeing.”

 That said, I created a ticket to escalate this internally and ensure we fix the typo.

Proposed Team:

 		AE Studio

 		Affected app:

 		TimeBack UI

 		Affected metrics:

 		Waste % in the Learning Report

 		Affected students:

 	* Wyatt Victore (wyatt.victore@2hourlearning.com)
 	* Mara Nevraumont - mara.nevraumont@2hourlearning.com
 	* Nova Victore - nova.victore@2hourlearning.com
 	* Ariel Martel - ariel.martel@2hourlearning.com
 	* Claudia Hobart - claudia.hobart@alpha.school
 	* Everest Nevraumont - everest.nevraumont@2hourlearning.com
 	* Daxon Hummel - daxon.hummel@2hourlearning.com
 	* August Pease - august.pease@2hourlearning.com
 	* Wayne Zou - wayne.zou@alpha.school
 	* Nate Evans - nate.evans@2hourlearning.com

 		Affected dates:

 		Session to date

 		Evidence:

 		 Grant is concerned that his students always have low waste percentages, and this doesn't seem to reflect their reality. For example, he highlights that Wyatt spent 30% of the day in the bathroom yesterday, but they still show 0% Waste in the dashboard.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/cqGRltsNIILSEDABeSIikjKzXaDOP5NY" height="901"]

Reviewing the help text in the dashboard, it makes sense that it only considers screen recordings, and if (speculating) it only takes available recordings as the 100% of time to analyze, it would make sense that it can't detect waste for times in which students may have turned off the computer, for example.

However, reviewing just a couple random recordings yesterday, you can easily see there is real waste captured in game film, which should be available to whatever data the dashboard uses based on the help text. Look at this clip from yesterday [https://main-worksmart-clips-0002md.s3.amazonaws.com/clips/2829453/1757617364851_52d1d28b-61cc-4040-8b42-a58f4d5437fb.mp4] in which the student can be seen visiting non-core-subjects-related sites during core skills time yesterday, for several minutes.
Of course, if this doesn't happen often enough and the dashboard rounds waste, it could still be valid that it displays 0% Waste, the point is we can't know right now and this is confusing for Guides.

We've received feedback in the past about how the Waste calculation is done for the Learning Report in Dash, but as far as we understand the dashboards in TimeBack are being built and maintained by AE Studio, so we would kindly need to hear from you how this works. Thank you!

 		Reason for Escalation:

 	* Please share how the Waste calculation is done and how it's supposed to work, use-cases, and/or any other useful context you can share. 
 	* Please confirm Waste is correct for Grant's students. 
 	* Feel free to share any key discussion points that Guide should be aware of (if any). 

 Thank you!  

 		Other notes:

 		Affected dates:

 		2025-09-10
2025-09-11

 		Evidence:

 		 We've recently received multiple reports of the same behavior from Guides and students across different campuses, for example in 60195058. This is a great cause of concern and confusion for affected students.

We're using Amelia Gabler (amelia.gabler@alpha.school) as an example below.

You can see the behavior clearly reflected in this clip from yesterday night [https://main-worksmart-clips-0002md.s3.amazonaws.com/clips/2836547/1757610636834_dd3d4ff8-19f8-4b8a-80aa-52fe229daaf8.mp4] (Windows clock in the bottom-right corner is in CT). Amelia Gabler's XP in VocabLoco starts at 80, increases to 85, decreases to 65, increases again to 75 after a refresh, and ends up at 70 at least at the end of the clip. Right now, the VocabLoco for 2025-09-10 is 80.

Assuming Caliper Events' timestamps are in UTC (as the documentation suggests), there don't seem to be events sent at the time the screen recording was captured, which would be around 1:29 am UTC of the 11th of September, 2025 .
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/x6ejeRa93OGOWR97mZAghUQyJ54ahpPk" height="698"]
 

Current XP in the TimeBack UI for VocabLoco on 09/10th/2025 appears to make sense if timestamps are in UTC, as there are 16 events each with 5 XP that would fall in the CT time zone.

 		Reason for Escalation:

 	* Please investigate and find the root cause. 
 	* Implement a fix. 
 	* Ensure XP displayed is accurate for any and all potentially affected students. 

Thank you! 

 		Other notes:

Even though the date is not visible in the screenshot below, you can confirm it from the URL.  Also, you can confirm from this screen recording [https://main-worksmart-clips-0002md.s3.amazonaws.com/clips/2830128/1757534124097_a9035795-7fb2-4d7c-bbd4-4c6d8d436e9e.mp4].

However, if you review Aksel's metrics for Writing / AlphaWrite in TimeBack for 2025-09-09 right now, you'll see only 75 XP. I'm in the time zone UTC-6, the student is in UTC-5, so time zone differences would definitely not explain the discrepancy, it is currently 15:32 CT (student's time zone) at the time of writing this. 
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/6sscmhmfRil1LTzk2rtoNuKGdZ19DLKZ" height="1078"]

 
Interestingly, as far as I can see, the Caliper events seem to indicate that Aksel should actually have 105 XP for this app/subject yesterday, as they have 7 events granting 15 XP each. [img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/6bSTemSL2hE9RIKW3WngfRRKRGz4JoJT" height="195"]

 	* Please implement a fix and ensure the data is correctly displayed for all potentially affected students. 

	* Kindly share if possible why this happened in the first place and what the fix was so that we can take this into account if any similar issues are reported in the future.  

 	* If this is not an issue, kindly share the full details to understand exactly why and what to expect so that we can effectively support Guides and Students who may become confused by this behavior. 

 Thank you!

linear_issue.description:
AI GENERATED

**Summary of the Conversation** 

* **Issue Raised:** Shepperd Pfiester reported that after completing 20 minutes on Membean with 90% accuracy, Timeback only recorded 10 minutes and 78% accuracy, with no XP awarded.
* **Initial Checks:** Support agents confirmed the discrepancy and noted similar issues on other dates (e.g., 44 minutes in Membean vs. 66 minutes in Timeback).
* **Actions Taken:**
  * The issue was escalated to the Superbuilders team for investigation.
  * Support confirmed that Timeback misreported the minutes and passed the case to a team member for resolution.
  * Later, a support agent observed that the correct data (20 minutes and 27 XP) appeared in the UI, suggesting a possible delay or UI issue.
  * The issue was further escalated to AE Studio, as the UI was not consistent and events had been sent for verification.
  * A possible timezone issue was mentioned, with events sent at 23:00 UTC.
* **Evidence Provided:** Screenshots and dashboard links were shared to verify the data.
* **Current Status:** The ticket is open and waiting on the third-party team (AE Studio) to resolve the UI inconsistency and ensure accurate data reflection in Timeback.

It looks like the numbers were just delayed getting to Timeback, but everything's showing up correctly now.

If anything like this happens again, feel free to reach out. We’ve got your back and want to make sure all your effort gets counted!

Keep up the great work,

Best regards,

posts.contents:
Dear Michael,

We’re pleased to confirm that the issue with Kennedy not receiving the Science placement test has been resolved.

Our Engineering team identified and fixed a logic bug that was incorrectly filtering out Science placement tests for Grade 2 students, even those who had mastered Reading. Additionally, a rounding issue in the mastery calculation was corrected.

As a result, as reported by Engineering, Kennedy and all other affected students are now correctly receiving their Science placement tests.

Thank you for your patience while we investigated and addressed this. Please let us know if there’s anything else we can assist you with.

Best regards,
Jan Paraniak
EDU Support Team

This ticket will stay open for one week unless you reply with "This ticket can be closed" or update the status to Completed in the portal. We will write to you again to remind you.

posts.contents:
The issue here appears to be related to a name change. Changes on the name on the Renaissance dashboard do not reflect on the Lalilo app. This causes a disperancy and the adapter is not able to detect student activity. So it would be just better keep the wrong name on the Renaissance, unless their support is contacted to handle this change on both apps. Renaissance is the platform where actual student rostering happens for Lalilo.  

 How it appears on Lalilo: 
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/Ghj4c2FgG8RALWkub08Wr5gByn6qSoq4" width="413" height="177"] 

 How it appears on Renaissance 
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/9M95CRIFtAxJEC1rXEzSTHoJFZCjateA" style="width: 61.95%;"] 

 Changed the name on the Renaissance dashboard to the wrong spelling of the student's last name, so their progress can be connected to their email address.

 	* Sept 8: ✅ +17 minutes (1020 seconds)

posts.contents:
Hi Harry, 

 Thank you for reaching out! You can actually set this up yourself through the UI. Here’s how: 

 	* Log into your admin account
 	* Go to Administration → Users
 	* Search for the user whose role you want to change
 	* In the Actions menu, click View Details
 	* Change the role to Aide for the school they’re in
 	* Add the students this aide will be responsible for

 This way, the guide will be able to view student learning metrics and impersonate the student.
Let me know if you run into any issues, I’ll be happy to help! 

 Best, 
 William

posts.contents:
Hi, Thanks for flagging this!

 The issue comes from the fact that our player does not support rendering <qti-catalog> tags. That’s why the audios are not working as expected. 

 The recommended approach is to use standard HTML <audio> tags within the QTI. These render correctly and are the supported way to include audio in XML content. 

 Just to clarify, we’re not responsible for the authoring or maintenance of the content itself on the platform. If you come across materials using unsupported tags like qti-catalog, the fix needs to come from the team or person who owns that specific piece of content.

 		The Guide reported there are discrepancies in goals between the daily and weekly views in the TimeBack UI. We've been able to replicate this.

See for Jacob Mooso (jacob.mooso@nextgenacademy.school), using Fast Math as an example (it may need to be a subject with non-standard goals).

The daily goals display as 4 mastered lessons (which equals to 20 weekly ones for a 5 day school week) and 10 XP. As far as we know, these numbers are correct.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/DKvvrgO4BAJbkPoVFP1oLkRHKlz44BBC" height="902"]

When reviewing the Learning Metrics page, the numbers are consistent for the Daily view (although I can't show all the goals in a single screenshot, but you get the point), with the daily goals being 10 minutes, 4 mastered units, and 10 XP.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/vx379iRhacPYvgq1UYqfxuZn0T8dguSH" width="783" height="688"]

However, in that same page, when switching to the Weekly view, the Daily goals appear to change; these are also not the Weekly goals being displayed, because they don't match the daily x5 as expected, it appears that the intention is that this also shows daily goals when you hover over the visuals, but it likely pulls data form elsewhere or is hardcoded and shows the default metrics for core subjects such as Language, Reading, or Math, which as far as we know are not the same for non-core subjects such as Fast Math or Writing.

Instead of 10 mins, 4 mastered units, and 10 XP, it now says 25 mins, 2 mastered units, and 25 XP.
[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/OeaYv0DBvi8GB1o6v55zB5MxboZ5GjCJ" height="905"]

 	* Please investigate and find the root cause. 
 	* Fix the issue.

posts.contents:
Hi Harry, 

 Thank you for reaching out! You can actually set this up yourself through the UI. Here’s how: 

 	* Log into your admin account
 	* Go to Administration → Users
 	* Search for the user whose role you want to change
 	* In the Actions menu, click View Details
 	* Change the role to Aide for the school they’re in
 	* Add the students this aide will be responsible for

 This way, the guide will be able to view student learning metrics and impersonate the student. 
 Let me know if you run into any issues, I’ll be happy to help! 

 Best, 
 William

Hi Harry,

 Thank you for reaching out! You can actually set this up yourself through the UI. Here’s how: 

 	* Log into your admin account
 	* Go to Administration → Users
 	* Search for the user whose role you want to change
 	* In the Actions menu, click View Details
 	* Change the role to Aide for the school they’re in
 	* Add the students this aide will be responsible for

This way, the guide will be able to view student learning metrics and impersonate the student. 
 Let me know if you run into any issues, I’ll be happy to help! 

 Best, 
 William

linear_issue.title: [60193744] Guides can't access their students anymore in TimeBack

posts.subject: Guides can't access their students anymore in TimeBack
posts.contents:
Dear Alonso,

Thank you for your patience. We have received the following update from the Time Back team:

Why did this happen? Is it intended?
The roles system was implemented with a higher granularity of roles for guides/parents. This change was intended and coordinated with Alpha.

What to expect moving forward?
Guides with roles (Lead Guide, Guide, Guide Assistant) will only see the students under their guidance, unless access is specifically requested and manually updated to extend visibility.

What are the differences between the different user roles?

	* Head of School – can see all students in their school
	* Lead Guide, Guide, Guide Assistant – can see all students under their guidance
	* Parent – can see their own children
	* Student – can only see their own data

What is the impact of the Organization assigned to a user?
The backend filters data using the organization assigned to a user. This prevents admins from specific orgs from seeing data from others. However, parent organizations can still view data from their child organizations. Direct guide-to-student relationships override this behavior.

Regarding your feature request (bulk user import):
At the moment, adding users remains a manual process. For a feature request to enable CSV or other bulk import methods, please reach out directly to our PMO Office:

	* Damon Young – damon.young@trilogy.com
	* Pascal Simpkins – pascal.simpkins@trilogy.com

As this request has now been addressed, we will go ahead and close this ticket. Please let us know if you have any additional questions or need further assistance.

Best regards,
EDU Support Team

posts.contents:
Hey, this thread was already answered by Edson on September 10th in Zendesk. Let me know if you have any further questions. Here’s the answer

 Hey there, here some answer for your questions: 
   

> Why did this happen? Is it intended?

 The roles system was implemented with a higher granularity of roles for guides/parents. It was intended and coordinated with Alpha. 
   

> What to expect moving forward?

 Guides with roles (Lead Guide, Guide, Guide Assistant) will see only the students under their guidance, unless requested and manually updated to see students out of this initial scope. 
   

> What are the differences between the different user roles?

 Head of School (can see all students for their school)
Lead Guide, Guide, Guide Assistant (can see all students under their guidance)
Parent (can see their kids)
Student (their own data) 
   

> What is the impact of the Organization assigned to a user?

 Our BE will filter data using the organization assigned to the user. This will be used to prevent admins from specific orgs from seeing data from other orgs (but remember that there is a hierarchy, so members of parent organizations can see data from child organizations). The direct relationship between guides and students override this behavior. 
   

> Finally, if adding users as described above is necessary from now on, I’d like to submit a Feature Request to be able to import data via CSV or other bulk methods, for example using student emails. In some cases, we need to enter tens of students and it’s not efficient to do so manually, one by one.

 Yes, a feature request should be made for this kind of feature. Right now, the process is manual and was done with the initial data provided to us.For the feature requests, please contact the PMO Office: 
   
 PMO Office Contacts 
 Damon Young - damon.young@trilogy.com
Pascal Simpkins - pascal.simpkins@trilogy.com

 We started receiving multiple reports today of Guides not being able to see their students in TimeBack anymore. Some of the reports received:

 	* vanessa.canavan@alpha.school and whitney.bunn@alpha.school - Only able to see the students in their guide group, but need to be able to see all students in the school. 
 	* anna.smiley@montessorium.school - Can't see any students, needs to see all students in Montessorium Cedar Park
 	* phoebe.gerbrecht@alpha.school - Can't see any students, need to access to New York students

The issues we've reviewed so far seem to be similar, in which the requester has a TimeBack account with “Aide” role. In an attempt to help, we've been going to Administration > Users > Locate the user and click on the ellipsis > View Details > Add Students

Could you please confirm:

 	* Why did this happen? Is it intended? 
 	* What to expect moving forward? 
 	* Is it OK that we've added students like this, or do we need to revert the changes/take any other action? 
 	* What are the differences between the different user roles? 
 	* What is the impact of the Organization assigned to a user? 

Finally, if adding users as described above is necessary from now on, I'd like to submit a Feature Request to be able to import data via CSV or other bulk methods, for example using student emails. In some cases, we need to enter tens of students and it's not efficient to do so manually, one by one.

Thank you.

 		 Kindly review and address. Thank you!

posts.contents:
Thank you for reaching out and for your patience as we investigate the issue with the “Essential Lessons Mastered vs. Target” report in the My Learning Report dashboard.

We understand how confusing and frustrating it can be to see sudden, unexplained changes in XP requirements, especially when setting learning goals and tracking student progress.

Our team is currently working on a full refactor of this report to ensure the data is accurate, reliable, and easy to understand. We’re collaborating with stakeholders to confirm which metrics should be displayed and how best to structure the report for clarity and consistency.

In the meantime, we recommend disregarding the XP requirement figures shown in the dashboard until the updated version is released. We’ll keep you informed as soon as improvements are live.
Thank you again for bringing this to our attention.

linear_issue.title: [228] [229] [60178692] Alpha Read - cross-out feature request
linear_issue.description:
> Hello Team,
>
> **Calie Garrett has suggested a feature in the Alpha Read app:**
>
> The ability for students to cross-out text that they have determined is NOT relevant to the question that they are answering.
>
> This would allow them to use deductive reasoning to find the answer, rather than relying on searching for the correct answer in a wall of text.
>
> **Calie shared the following:**
>
> > Oftentimes it's visually helpful to be able to cross out information that students are trying to either ignore, is irrelevant, or is clearly not the correct answer.  So it's helpful to be able to cross out answer choices as well as text that students either want to ignore to visually keep from including.For example, if a question is asking for a student to identify the thesis of a text, students might want to be able to cross out sentences that they can tell are either supporting details or conclusion statements, that way they eliminate them visually from their available options. It's just as powerful of a tool as highlighting.You know how sometimes it's easier to identify what we DON'T want than it is what we do? 
>
> Currently, AlphaRead offers the ability to highlight text, using left click and drag.
>
> The ability to cross-out text (Or highlight in Red) could be added using right click and drag.
>
> Additionally, highlighting only persists until a new highlight is started. It may be beneficial for the highlighting to persist. A checkbox could be introduced to enable persistent highlighting/crossing-out of text.
>
> This should be considered as a feature request, which would need to be forwarded to Andy and Kathryn.
>
> I wanted to run it by you first, to check for any technical limitations, and to get the Reading DRI perspective on if this would be a beneficial addtion, or if there's anything else that should be considered.
>
> Thank you very much for your input!
> 
> Ticket URL: [https://timeback.zendesk.com/agent/#/tickets/228](https://timeback.zendesk.com/agent/#/tickets/228)

posts.contents:
Dear Ashley,

Thank you for your patience while we investigated Atticus's Timeback Dash enrollment issues.

Language Enrollment Status:

Unfortunately, we currently do not have language courses available for grades 3-5 in Timeback. However, these courses may be available as early as next week. We will monitor this and ensure Atticus is properly enrolled once the courses become available.

Writing Enrollment Clarification: Regarding the multiple AlphaWrite enrollments you mentioned - this is actually the correct setup. Atticus completed Sentences G3 and naturally progressed to Sentences G4. He has now been enrolled in Paragraphs G3, which is the appropriate next step in his writing progression. The grade-level course progression is: Sentences G3 → Paragraphs G3, Sentences G4 → Paragraphs G4, etc. While he is welcome to continue his work in Sentences G4, he won't be able to test-out of Writing G3 before completing Paragraphs G3.

We understand your concern about Atticus's high MAP scores and appropriate grade-level placement. Once the Language courses become available, we will ensure he is enrolled at the appropriate G4 level as determined by his placement tests.

We will continue to monitor this situation and provide updates as soon as the Language courses are available.

Best regards,
Randall Shawver
EDU Support Team

[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/exe9mQJgnS2oeFTbtaBMVoTo9LLFxnSy" style="width: 50.24%;"]

Verifying with the DRI, Lalilo should only be categorized under Language:

[img src="https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/media/url/puXjINJUlOkAtKrZpS7Dk98fOR80Y2D6" width="633"]

 		Reason for Escalation:
 		  To fix past data, resend events to overwrite or balance the originals. For example, if 10 XP was sent by mistake, send -10 XP, then send a new event with the correct values. Make sure to use the same event.object.id and updated metrics so it’s treated as an update.

In general terms, all that is needed is to send an event with the exact same payload as the previous one and change only the metrics.

To do this, the event you want to replace must first be located. Use the Caliper API to fetch the event before resubmitting

API: https://caliper.alpha-1edtech.com/scalar#tag/caliper-events/get/caliper/events

Important Considerations

Replacing past events introduces risks that must be carefully managed:

• No Official Mechanism (Until Now): Up to this point, we did not have an official mechanism to update past metrics. This means consumers may not expect event updates.

• Consistency of Processing: We are depending on all consumers to process and aggregate metrics the same way we do. If any system counts or sums metrics differently, inconsistencies will arise.

• Risk of Divergence: Without alignment across all parties, updates may create more problems than solutions, leading to mismatched totals across systems.

 		Other notes:
 		 AE Studio suggested an escalation

posts.contents:
SUMMARY OF THE ISSUE

 Ticket Details: 

 	* Requester: Annie Hoaldridge-Dopkins (anne.dopkins@alpha.school)
 	* Student: Ethan Stromfeld (ID: 2509, email: ethan.stromfeld@2hourlearning.com)
 	* Issue: Lalilo's time was incorrectly registered under Reading instead of Language subject
 	* Date Reported: August 27, 2025
 	* Product: EDU (Alpha School)

WHAT HAPPENED

 	* Initial Report: Annie reported that Ethan's Lalilo time was showing up under Reading instead of Language in reports
 	* Investigation: The EDU Support team escalated this to multiple teams:

 	* First to AE Studio
 	* Then to Superbuilders (the integration team)

 	* Root Cause: The Lalilo adapter was sending incorrect Caliper events with wrong subject, sensor, and app information
 	* Technical Details: The system was using event subject when course subject was missing, but the adapter needed to send correct events

RESOLUTION

 As of September 2, 2025: Lalilo events have been updated to correctly send the subject as Language instead of Reading. 

WHAT THIS MEANS

 	* ✅ Going forward: New Lalilo sessions will display correctly under Language in reports
 	* ⚠️ Historical data: Past incorrect data remains, but the system now has a mechanism to handle updates
 	* 📊 Reports: Future reports should show accurate subject categorization

CUSTOMER RESPONSE

 The ticket is ready to be sent to the customer with the message that the issue has been resolved and new sessions will display correctly going forward. This appears to be a successful resolution where the integration team fixed the data source issue, ensuring future Lalilo usage will be properly categorized under the correct subject area.

posts.subject: Wrong AlphaMath Fluency XP for Jesse Crain
posts.contents:
Dear Ree,

Thank you for your patience while we worked with the AlphaMath team on this. The difference in XP granted to Jesse is due to how AlphaMath Fluency distinguishes between active time and waste time.

	* Active time is the time Jesse spent productively working in the app — answering questions, thinking, typing responses, or transitioning between questions (including up to 15 seconds of page load time).
	* Waste time is any remaining time where no progress was made, such as being idle on a problem, pausing without answering, or leaving the app open.

In Jesse’s session, although about 20 minutes were recorded on video, the system detected only ~8 minutes as active time. Since XP is awarded at 1 XP per active minute (adjusted for accuracy), this explains why Jesse received fewer XP than expected.

You can go over further details here in the internal guide, if you have access to it: AlphaMath XP Guide [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1S0CSTgNIX_TnacE0oxQgxtPnqq1aG6J129gZUWH53P4/edit?tab=t.0&utm_source=chatgpt.com].

We hope this clarifies the discrepancy. Please let us know if you’d like us to review Jesse’s data on other dates or if you have additional concerns.

Best regards,
Syed Haider
EDU Support Team

Thank you for your patience while we worked on this issue with the relevant team. Please note that the difference in XP granted to Jesse seems to stem from the difference between active and waste time.

Since antipatterns cannot be directly detected, AMF relies on the assumption that time spent in answering questions (thinking, typing, transitions) is “active” and the remaining time is waste, after allowing for time spent in typing, moving between pages and app loading times. Based on the screen recordings, we believe that even though Jesse spent 20 minutes working, most of that time was wasted, based on this rubric. 

 You can read further details regarding how FastMath works here [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1S0CSTgNIX_TnacE0oxQgxtPnqq1aG6J129gZUWH53P4/edit?tab=t.0]. We hope this helps. In case there are any further questions or concerns, please let us know. We are always happy to help.

Dear Eric,

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated the issue regarding Science courses on TimeBack for the St James Performance Academy students.

We’re pleased to share that the academic team has confirmed that all students now have accounts set up in the app. Those who met the eligibility criteria—having mastered G2 Reading and completed the Science placement test—have already been enrolled in their Science courses on TimeBack. Please see the attached screenshot of Mason Romeo Timeback, which shows a science skill recommendation from the app MobyMax. 

For the remaining students, once they achieve G2 or higher Reading proficiency and complete the Science placement test, they will also be enrolled accordingly. If you or the guide have any additional questions or run into issues, please don't hesitate to reach out.

Thank you.

Best regards,
Syed Haider
EDU Support Team

posts.subject: Science courses are not showing in Timeback for St James Performance Academy students
posts.contents:
Dear Eric,

Thank you very much for reaching out to the Alpha support team. I understand that you are concerned about Science courses not showing in Timeback for the St James Performance Academy students.

We have determined that, at the moment, there is no auto-enrollment mapped for Science courses in Subject Tracks. This means that, even if students complete the Science placement tests, the Academics team still needs to manually enroll them in the desired courses. We also confirmed that auto-enrollment for Science is planned for release next week and is expected to be fully tested and available on Monday, September 8th. This new feature will be gated by the G2 Reading test.

An escalation has been made requesting that the students be enrolled in the appropriate science course.

Please let me know if you have any questions or need any assistance in the meantime.

Best regards,
Yahya Miled
Alpha Support Team

posts.subject: Bug in an AlphaRead article
posts.contents:
Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for flagging the issue with Kaiden’s AlphaRead article “The Sword in the Lake.”

We wanted to reach out to share that our Development Team identified the root cause and has now resolved the problem.

Question 3 didn’t have a correct answer properly configured, which caused the app to loop and fail to provide feedback after submission. The grading logic for Question 3 has been corrected and the article now progresses normally and provides the right feedback.

Please let us know if Kaiden runs into the problem again or if you notice anything else unusual.

Thank you.

Best regards,
Benito Hall
EDU Support Team

This ticket will stay open for one week unless you reply with "This ticket can be closed" or update the status to Completed in the portal. We will write to you again to remind you.

posts.contents:
Hi Taskforce,

Thank you for reporting this issue with Kaiden's AlphaRead article experience. I'm pleased to inform you that our development team has successfully identified and resolved the problem.

What was fixed:

	* The question looping issue in "The Sword in the Lake" article has been resolved
	* Question 3's grading system has been corrected
	* The application now properly progresses through questions and provides appropriate feedback

Root cause: The issue was caused by Question 3 not having a correct answer properly configured in the system, which caused the application to malfunction and loop back to the same question.

Next steps: Kaiden should now be able to complete the article without experiencing the looping issue. If you encounter any similar problems in the future, please don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.

Thank you for your patience while we investigated and resolved this issue. We appreciate you bringing this to our attention so we could improve the AlphaRead experience for all students.

Best regards,
Randall Shawver
EDU Support Team

ADDITIONAL CONTEXT?

 They're in Alpha High School, using timeback 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf3TFUvCwo_JAOozpeu4pa5PBxwcQ4HFDikAYfqvG3HQEaGprdmsQxNc9SieC4OO4xG_Tu9x_9_ANazF6nDL4SCqKvP3m0I70LEA-VI4DKV0hGtxVc1yeuJYE3rpasNSYGVKbbFkQ?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="617" height="99"] 

 Checked the recordings, but there are no recent ones: 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfLzqCSjIqPocLGBSruvXnYbJcorcSOpNRrcsZ-sqXJaHcbPK2W-_PgxqkKljpLuc2FVbrh4zhrDkPPE8iosdUuvQmATRpeKv9ioVfLIdQg6IOhc1R6rgCLm0uPSep9WSNiKaYhFQ?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1632" height="599"] 

 Raised https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/agent/conversations/60178012 to investigate that. 

 Timeback shows 88% - In progress 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfnuVxTI3M8St8im1ASu8hpIX1dIA7Eoy4mTmsp6wGLodY3D7nwKfMMOiuW9sydki-1wGpoxRL50tH2HZYrdYDofzHyLLNKqeCLH-yJaahgkKvcvQ4XsuaC__i9t3Yw7aEqOf2vRA?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1244" height="304"] 

 Impersonated, confirmed that the exercise was completed: 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfHjgt24ktX3qBAHGyA2Bp8VPizwrTNg-VjKZV1KHp5iH4NmRBZhM-GOS-F61ed5KnTiduzP-Q3pfrQfvdzWqCNAeK178KtlkyYD_1VKMoU9xBliQGacGJd8e5u8VKqYNO9eOnt?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1593" height="572"] 

 But the Alpha Read Dashboard only shows that article to complete, and they can’t select another article from AlphaRead: 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc5TlD9ZDSnYyh8q14EgdZLZV_xFgiXpt0VzGv1oSihnSvlNCeH0UroZyCr_HUVoW6CDPLtaoCdgqzl0jvYd8vGON0Yk8Hr2KxA9SPgkGN8F8UIP_eLFll-VQTdpw0kCjOLaWNTPQ?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1630" height="515"] 

 The article should be removed from timeback regardless of the %, as noted on this article: https://support.alpha.school/article/31530-how-to-check-if-a-student-has-mastered-all-their-alpharead-articles-on-dash 
 “An article is complete once all questions have been answered and should be removed from the student's recommendations as they have no way to try it again, regardless of the final score/accuracy” 

 So I should escalate to AE Studio for fixing. 

 I also wanted to unlock the next lesson like in dash so the student is not blocked and can work on the next assignment. There is an “Unlock content” checkbox: 
 [img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf_FDJf3Pv105juZ7azZuWqkcmnhfYfaxhVCp-wD9YQPCaokocw9I5vG-yA6I15pAobWPDxjfDCuJFAQynMLisdsZYIOS8YaKlRR5IpCLuGSrDGXkuwjWOKTkgmzkYIA0UorvN6QQ?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1211" height="478"]  

 Checking the box selects “ungreys” the other articles, but there is no save button. When the page is refreshed, this reverses. 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcFDke2jRglVMHU9755p4ieH83Qi6fBX5NfPtAcD4fmd3HrmeWsG0CCbSvOObxMWRBiZian5L6gBNBVNXJiK4FYSPHcIjbLLOPe--_7QGy7Y9zfGpgTUC3fvKKbDHV-uhR991Decg?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1264" height="500"] 

 I even tried the reset lesson plan icon. But resetting it does absolutely nothing. 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfL9idHFdLlnUJmeVbtmNIRc4dAOXLj-A0r1zB4DGb-ebaVaRKaecYGG3fsK7BvUxcPCzQxbZ7EVJivxo8pnW-92DS0AJL8jm17C_XZ4zRxeA1e_svXb153UGSkuhTKzw3AaXjpFQ?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="247" height="104"] 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeM3_SSEl6ecBcCd12qbMW9TZRzFJyZTsN_AoR9nsCt9F3Gz8zy1EyaaEyDQPGWh0MyiNta7cp6_shTl3H3_ozjcT8OsCUOxih2XOMFnyR-FnYzyDjhnwbefPvjq1bGAicj7cjh?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="544" height="186"] 

 I have impersonated the student to see what they see in timeback and Alpha Read, there is no change before and after “unlocking content” and “resetting lesson plan”. 

 I also found that even though it’s greyed out, the students can still click on the button and it will take them directly to the exercise, which they can complete: 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeHQRaZF25Bko0S3l1o2pVO-oSqwPBoBzHjQOz0L7JE1lumtyuc1sxOTuzhrTrBRELMmuY_sqstG3Ys5VdWFHn3jTDv9-q2D-ED9GOop1xjBeB6k6P8k6RgarBgu-SEpNHW_LRQcA?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1259" height="494"] 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdIZG09H8VWLFBa-rKGU8DQFpG3OZXUad0kkI9ipvv_WfCf6LZkK1ex2K1hTP77bc90U9hgJQEltfqJX31omj5zP2DPa_8BZoefBOgMNrXjgtiRT_aqbxNjctkzk0ouJ-PWJxHK_A?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1631" height="571"] 

 While on AlphaRead, locked activities cannot be selected: 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeod-IivptgP1iSqSkA2BQVZ5hlOe0kUtwVYhrHz1-GRuUTyewyNupBC25e_aqme1SrjfsRy0vKWgBC5jUVSib1GtsC8Do951tiGSXpyJ9xOajzUfA4rGzA0EcdKePmHEeQ9krOqA?key=FDF_utsq9V3S7S3KiYtGBA" width="1250" height="682"] 

 I was about to connect to the powerpath database to investigate further:  https://support.alpha.school/article/31912-connecting-to-the-powerpath-database but decided not to, as there appears to be something wrong with the dashboards; we should have a way to unblock next lessons. 

 Created https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/agent/conversations/60178018 to report the above to AE Studio and ask them how to unblock lessons.

posts.contents:
We released this improvement on Sep 2 (to allow processing events older than 48h) as planned, but had to revert it after identifying some issues. Adjustments were made, and as of last Friday all events were reprocessed. All learning metrics should now be correct.

 For Samantha Hilton’s case, however, after checking the learning reports page and our database we did not find any records of events from Amplify. We should ask them to make sure they indeed emit the events, and once this is done, they should appear automatically.

posts.contents:
Just to add to the previous message.

In general terms, all that is needed is to send an event with the exact same payload as the previous one and change only the metrics.
To do this, the event you want to replace must first be located. Use the Caliper API to fetch the event before resubmitting
API: https://caliper.alpha-1edtech.com/scalar#tag/caliper-events/get/caliper/events

Important Considerations
Replacing past events introduces risks that must be carefully managed:

• No Official Mechanism (Until Now): Up to this point, we did not have an official mechanism to update past metrics. This means consumers may not expect event updates.
• Consistency of Processing: We are depending on all consumers to process and aggregate metrics the same way we do. If any system counts or sums metrics differently, inconsistencies will arise.
• Risk of Divergence: Without alignment across all parties, updates may create more problems than solutions, leading to mismatched totals across systems.

linear_issue.description:
[Kayako ticket.](https://central-supportdesk.kayako.com/agent/conversations/60178018)

On this ticket some questions were raised by the reporter. The first issue is that a student got stuck in an Alpha Read article and they wanted to unblock them. 

Followed by the first issue they raised questions about how the Admin functions `Unlock Content` and `Reset lesson plan works`. For these questions is just a matter of explaining that these actions only affect the admin user and not the impersonated student.

The second issue is a bug, they found that students have a way to click on a disabled button and access an article that is not supposed to be worked on, this should be fixed.

posts.subject: Questions about TimeBack and AlphaRead
posts.contents:
Dear Andres,

Please find answers for your queries:
1 - How does the “Unlock content” checkbox work?
This checkbox, along with show past checkbox and the reset content button are admin features, they will only make effect for you current browser session, it won't reach the student.

2 - What does Reset lesson plan do? We used it, but nothing happened.
It resets the lesson plan for the Admin user.

3 - We found that even though it’s greyed out, the students can still click on the button and it will take them directly to the exercise.
We'll be releasing a fix for it on the Aug 29th release.

Best regards,
Qasim Ali
EDU Support Team

We have checked in with the relevant teams and the mastery units are not currently tracked for AlphaRead articles which is why you do not see the units although the XP has been awarded to the student.

posts.contents:
What is your proposed action? 
 Send to external team 

 Additional Context: 
 SC: 
 Subject: Feature Request: Enable Mastery Tracking in AlphaRead 
 To: damon.young@trilogy.com, pascal.simpkins@trilogy.com 
-------------------------

 Dear Damon and Pascal, 
 We’d like to submit a feature request related to mastery tracking in the AlphaRead application. 
 Context:
Currently, AlphaRead awards XP for completed articles based on performance but does not track mastered units (MUs). This design differs from legacy systems (such as Dash and Timeback), where articles completed with ≥80% accuracy were considered mastered. This mismatch is causing confusion for users, as Timeback expects to display mastered units but receives none from AlphaRead. 
 Feature Request:
Implement mastery tracking in AlphaRead, where an article is marked as mastered if the user achieves a score of 80% or higher. These mastered units should be reflected both internally and in Timeback reporting 
 =============================================================== 
 What is the PR to the customer? 

 Dear Joshua, 

 We've submitted a feature request to the PMO Office to enable mastery tracking in AlphaRead, specifically marking articles with 80%+ accuracy as mastered units. 

 We’ve escalated this to Damon Young and Pascal Simpkins and will keep you updated on any developments. 

 Best regards,

How does this affect the student? :
 		Mastered units are not being tracked in AlphaRead, even though students earn XP for completing articles with high accuracy. This creates a mismatch between AlphaRead and Timeback, where mastered units are expected to appear.

 		What investigation did CS carry out? :
 		AE Studio confirmed that AlphaRead sets mastered units to 0 by design and only logs XP. Reportedly, there is no definition of mastery for AlphaRead, thus mastery does not appear to be tracked in the Timeback UI.

posts.contents:
Checking this ticket as it's 16 days old now and seems to be stuck. In short:  

 	* Guide would like access to historical Check Charts data. 
 	* This was previously owned by Dash (Learning Engineering), but it has since been removed from the system and handed over to superbuilders (specifically, to Benjamin Vizy) so that the data was imported and integrated into TimeBack. 
 	* This was done, but in a different TimeBack: the Superbuilders Team's TimeBack as opposed as the current AE Studio TimeBack everyone is using. 

	* The team who owns the current version of TimeBack (AE Studio) doesn't know how/where in the database the data was stored.  

 	* This indicates the decision was unilateral, and the implementation is ready as expected only in the Superbuilders Team's TimeBack, and not in AE Studio's TimeBack. 

 As such, for the time being there is no point in chasing this escalation anymore. The AE Studio team can keep developing their version of TimeBack with whatever specifications they've been receiving from Top Management/Academics; if this includes Check Charts, they should coordinate with Benjamin directly, but for the time being it's clear Check Charts are not available in AE Studio's TimeBack.

posts.subject: Fast math Error
posts.contents:
Hi Blake,

Great question! Here’s what’s going on:

FastMath is set up to compare how many units you did with the “goal” of just 2 units. Since you actually did 316 units, the system does the math like this:
316 ÷ 2 = 158  →  158 × 100 = 15,800%

So the huge number (15,800%) isn’t a mistake — it’s just how the system shows progress. The percentage looks funny because the goal is so small (2 units), and you did a lot more than that.

What really matters is that you’re making excellent progress. The big percentage is just the computer’s way of showing that you went way beyond the goal.

Keep up the great work — the numbers may look strange, but your effort is what counts most!

Best regards,
Qasim Ali
EDU Support Team

The recommended units to be mastered is set to 2 on TimebackUI as a default. Looking at the events in Caliper sent for fastmath, I am unsure how they are calculating mastered units, but the numbers are much higher than 2. For example, looking at this event in caliper with id: 436968, we can see the masteredUnits is set to 58.

For Wednesday, 8/13, there are 18 activities logged and 9 of those have a total masteredUnits of 316. The following day, 8/14, there are 8 events with 4 of those events combining for a total of 127 masteredUnits.

All events are logged, Blake is working through the exercises. The masteredUnits completed for FastMath is much higher than 2 which is why we are seeing very large percentage show up on when looking at the weekly view.

These events can be verified by going here: https://us-east-1.quicksight.aws.amazon.com/sn/accounts/147371647228/dashboards/db0b2284-afa2-4b67-b0cf-989ed2ab21e4?directory_alias=alpha-quicksights
